title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 63
paragraphs: When Themistocles spoke thus, Eurybiades was persuaded to change his mind; and, I think, he changed his mind chiefly from fear that the Athenians might depart and abandon them if he moved the ships to the Isthmus — for if the Athenians left them and went, the rest would no longer be able to fight the enemy. So he chose this course: to remain where they were and decide matters there in a sea-battle.
